subject: how to run multiple installations of shiny package with 1 installation of Shiny Server Pro and R?

messages.author: f1a78b77bed56547
messages.subject: how to run multiple installations of shiny package with 1 installation of Shiny Server Pro and R?
parts:
Hi,

We have an installation of Shiny Server Pro, R, and Shiny. We have a bunch of Shiny apps that have been developed, validated, and are in "production". We need to keep these apps frozen at the current versions of Server, R, and Shiny.

I'm developing a new app that depends strongly on a bug fix in a new version of the shiny package. Is it possible, and how may I install and use the new version of shiny package along with keeping the old version?

Eventually this will become the same issue with R, and the Shiny Server Pro itself. How may I have apps on a per app basis run in different versions of R, and ultimately Shiny Server Pro?

Jonathan

messages.author: 3da48b33a2f506a9
messages.subject: Re: how to run multiple installations of shiny package with 1 installation of Shiny Server Pro and R?
parts:
Jonathan,

There are a variety of ways you can do this. First I want to point you to this article which gives general guide lines on how to manage libraries:

https://support.rstudio.com/hc/en-us/articles/215733837-Managing-libraries

For Shiny Server Pro you have the option to define r_path at granular levels. Please refer to this section of Admin Guide:

http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#r_path

You can also use exec_supervisor and pass in specific R library paths at different granular levels. Please refer to this section of Admin Guide:

http://rstudio.github.io/shiny-server/latest/#program-supervisors

And you also have the option to use packrat projects. An individual application could be a packrat project, tied to specific versions of all dependent packages, and deployed to Shiny Server Pro which will use those versions.

Hope this helps. Feel free to open support ticket if you are a Shiny Server Pro customer.

Best,
Fereshteh
